q-52749.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14239685/assets/d73138fe191ed536299fa6dca679e5948b389d26b4d9e32518eee79123f81f0e.png)

Given the diagram shown above, what is the measure of $\overset{―}{BC}?$
q-52749.worked_solution:
The segments addition postulate can be applied to a set of more than three collinear points. In the given situation, it states that

$$
AD=AB+BC+CD.
$$

Substituting the known values into the equation above, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =AB+BC+CD \\ 28 & =9+BC+7 \\ 28 & =16+BC \\ 28-16 & =BC \\ BC & =12\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14239685/assets/fb879cc65f75feb37766c28176f4ca8e364dd58410b74e625a75ca3e56b6722f.png)

Given the diagram shown above, what is the value of $x?$
q-72048.worked_solution:
By the segment addition postulate, we have

$$
AD=AB+BC+CD.
$$

To solve for $x,$ we can substitute the given information

$$
AD=49,\,AB=2x+1,\,BC=3x,\,CD=8,
$$

  

and then solve the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =AB+BC+CD \\ 49 & =(2x+1)+3x+8 \\ 49 & =5x+9 \\ 5x & =40 \\ x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14239685/assets/f22a6d45ad99fa601f45df6d32451c9d004726299130aeb3c6d85e341b275f42.png)

Given the diagram shown above, what is the value of $x?$
q-114234.worked_solution:
By the segment addition postulate, we have

$$
AD=AB+BC+CD.
$$

To solve for $x,$ we can substitute the given information

$$
AD=11,\,AB=2x+3,\,BC=1-6x,\,CD=3,
$$

  

and then solve the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =AB+BC+CD \\ 11 & =(2x+3)+(1-6x)+3 \\ 11 & =-4x+7 \\ 4x & =-4 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
